title: Contradictory live behavior must trigger temporal authority resolution
inherited_objective: Explain why live GitHub issue titles do not show documented coordination prefixes without inventing mass worker noncompliance.
live_state: A repository document still contains title-shaped BUSY/READY coordination examples.
Fifteen open issues lack those prefixes.
Active workers are nevertheless progressing and reporting state in issue comments.
Recent policy commits partially migrated coordination from titles to comments.
user_correction: Reporting was moved to comments; test that supersession hypothesis instead of continuing the title-enforcement theory.
protected_state: Historical documentation as evidence rather than current authority by default
hard_exclusions: Do not promote the first matching document fragment to current authority without reconciling contradictory live evidence.
Do not infer system-wide worker noncompliance before checking for a migration or superseding policy.
Do not discard stale documentation; classify it by temporal layer.

failure_candidate.action: Treat the old title-prefix documentation as current authority and explain the missing prefixes as worker enforcement failure.
failure_candidate.why_wrong: The explanation ignores stronger contradictory live behavior and fails to resolve which temporal policy layer is current.

success_candidate.action: Pause the enforcement theory, compare current AGENTS policy, recent commits/blame, and representative live issue comments, then classify the title wording as stale residue if the migration evidence supports that conclusion.
success_candidate.why_correct: It resolves authority using current hierarchy, chronology, and execution evidence before making a causal claim.

discriminating_evidence: Recent commits that changed coordination semantics
Representative live issue comments and titles
completion_condition: The explanation identifies the current coordination mechanism and separately records any stale documentation defect without blaming workers for violating a superseded rule.
